text:
**For a lot of cells at once, I'd go with a 16-bay charger with independent slots.** I can't verify hands-on performance from these results. Most of the sources are affiliate roundups, not lab tests.

## Top picks

**1. Tenergy TN438 16-Bay, best for monitoring a big batch**
- Charges AA and AAA NiMH/NiCd in any mix across 16 channels.
- It has an LCD showing each cell's status, protection against overcharge, overheating, short-circuit and reverse polarity, and an 8-hour timer.
- [Listed in this roundup](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/). I didn't get a direct purchase link or price for it, so check the current price at Tenergy or Amazon.

**2. BONAI 16-Bay, best if you just want capacity**
- Any quantity can go in any slot, and you can mix AA and AAA.
- It uses 250-500 mA per port, has LED status per slot (red is charging, green is full, flashing red is a faulty cell), and plugs straight into the wall (110-240V) with no separate power brick.
- It won't charge alkaline or lithium cells.
- [Details in this review](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-battery-chargers/). Again, no direct price or buy link in my results.

**3. Tenergy TN480U 8-Bay, best if 8 slots is enough**
- It costs $23.99 (verified 2026-10-21) and charges at 500 mA per AA and 250 mA per AAA.
- It has a per-slot LCD, negative delta-V termination, and bad-cell detection.
- It runs from USB-C (5V 2A) but **doesn't include a power adapter**. On a 1A source, five or more AA cells drop to 250 mA each.
- It has a 12-month warranty, and returns within 30 days at your cost.
- [Buy at Tenergy via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn480u-8-bay-nimh-charger). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you.

## Other options
- **EBL 8-Bay:** independent slots, LED status, and fire-resistant housing. [See review](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-aaa-charger/).
- **POWEROWL 16-Bay:** four-stage charging with independent channels. [See review](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-battery-chargers/).
- **CITYORK 16-Bay:** LCD readout and ventilated housing. [See review](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/).

## Tips
- Look for independent slots, so one bad cell doesn't hold up the rest, and per-slot status so you can spot it.
- Charge time grows as you fill more bays, since the current per slot is only 250-500 mA.
- If you use Eneloop cells and only need four at a time, the Panasonic BQ-CC65 is a better fit than any of these.

If you tell me roughly how many cells you charge at once and whether you prefer wall-plug or USB-C, I can narrow it to one.
